cards.text: Paul the apostle is finishing his letter to Timothy, the one he calls his beloved child (2 Timothy 1:2). Paul's in chains (2 Timothy 1:16), and he just said the time of his departure is at hand (2 Timothy 4:6). Now it gets personal, and Paul asks Timothy to make every effort to come to him quickly, which is apostle for DROP EVERYTHING.

cards.question: Paul wants Timothy there fast, because Demas, one of his fellow workers (Philemon 1:24), has deserted him and gone to Thessalonica. What pulled Demas away?

cards.text: Crescens has gone to Galatia, and Titus, Paul's partner and fellow worker (2 Corinthians 8:23), to Dalmatia. Paul's keeping track of people all over the map, and friend, I lose track of my timers in ONE kitchen.

cards.question: With Demas, Crescens and Titus gone, who is the only one still with Paul?
Only Luke, the beloved physician (Colossians 4:14), is with Paul. Paul tells Timothy to get Mark, who once traveled with Paul and Barnabas (Acts 12:25), and bring him along. Why does Paul want Mark?

answers.text: He is useful in the ministry
He has money for the trip

cards.text: Back in Acts, Paul thought it best not to take Mark along, because Mark had deserted them in Pamphylia (Acts 15:38). Now Paul's asking for him by name, and friend, as a stamper who got called out of the back of a junk drawer, I LOVE a callback.

cards.question: Paul mentions Tychicus, one of Paul's travel companions (Acts 20:4). True or false: like Demas, Tychicus has now deserted Paul.

cards.text: Tychicus is still on the job, friend. Paul sent him to Ephesus himself.

Then Paul gets practical: when Timothy comes, bring the cloak Paul left with Carpus at Troas, and his scrolls, especially the parchments. Friend, even an apostle has a list of stuff he left at somebody's house.
Then comes a new name: Alexander the coppersmith. Paul says Alexander did him great harm.

cards.question: Paul says the ___ will repay Alexander according to his deeds.
Paul tells Timothy to beware of Alexander too. Why?

answers.text: He has strongly opposed their message
He has spread lies about Timothy
He has stirred up the city leaders

cards.text: Now Paul looks back at his first defense. Friend, a moment like that shows you who's really in your corner.

cards.question: At Paul's first defense, everyone ___ him, but the Lord ___ by him.
True or false: Paul wants the people who deserted him at his first defense to be charged for it.

cards.text: Everybody walked out on him, and Paul's response is: "May it not be charged against them." Friend, I once sulked over a cracked cookie for a WHOLE afternoon, and I'm the one who cracked it.

cards.question: The Lord stood by Paul and strengthened him so the message would be fully proclaimed. Who would get to hear it?

cards.text: Then Paul says he was delivered from the mouth of the lion. Friend, the scariest thing I ever faced was somebody cleaning out the junk drawer I used to live in, and this man's talking about a LION'S MOUTH.

cards.question: Paul's already been rescued once, and he says the Lord will rescue him from every evil action. Looking ahead, what else is he sure the Lord will do for him?

answers.text: Bring him safely into the heavenly kingdom
Free him from his chains in this life
Give him many more years of preaching

cards.text: Then Paul says, "To Him be the glory forever and ever. Amen." Chains on, a lion's mouth behind him, and he's STILL giving glory.

Then the greetings start: Paul tells Timothy to greet Prisca and Aquila, whom Paul calls his fellow workers in Christ Jesus (Romans 16:3), and the household of Onesiphorus, the man who often refreshed Paul and wasn't ashamed of his chains (2 Timothy 1:16). He adds that Erastus, one of his helpers (Acts 19:22), has remained at Corinth.

cards.question: Paul also mentions Trophimus, who once traveled with him (Acts 20:4). Why isn't Trophimus with Paul now?

answers.text: He was left sick in Miletus

cards.question: Paul asks it again: make every effort to come. This time he adds a deadline. Timothy should come before ___.

cards.text: Then Eubulus, Pudens, Linus, Claudia and all the brothers send Timothy greetings. It's like when one person says hello in the group chat and your phone buzzes for an HOUR.

cards.question: Paul's closing his letter to Timothy. True or false: grace is part of the last words of this letter.

cards.text: Paul signs off: "The Lord be with your spirit. Grace be with you all." From a man in chains, the last thing he leaves them with is grace.
